        "All 346 owned diff lines across four paths were read, including the full 166-line test. Drag-over accepts message/rfc822 metadata only for a non-server filing target. Drop iterates each URL, creates an AttachmentInfo instance, awaits each import, catches each failure and then awaits folder refresh. The producer stores metadata separately per item, but this receiver takes type/name/URI from index zero for every item. The single-item test does not establish mixed-selection behavior.",
        "The production importer fetches through the instance, normalizes CR/LF variants to CRLF in 8 KiB chunks, writes a uniquely named 0600 file under a 0700 process temp directory and awaits copyFileMessageAsync. The copy promise uses onStopCopy success/error and marks the imported message read. Folder refresh is a separate IMAP-only status callback. No native fetch, IMAP APPEND, malformed MIME or large-message performance result is inferred.",
        "The owned original removes the temp file only after successful write/copy. Accepted importToFolder has later try/finally cleanup from the separate Copy To phase, and setupTempFile is later public rather than private. Those later changes are not credited to this initial drag/drop landing. Delete-on-exit registration is a fallback, not proof of prompt failure cleanup.",

Its four assertions have nonempty should messages and check a source header, routed fake call, destination count and subject. The test does not invoke the production fetch, normalization or temp cleanup and does not check drag-over, invalid targets, multiple items or rejection cleanup. Its full blob is identical at the fixed accepted revision.",

Comments describe chunk/line-ending constraints, but the performance/collection wording is not a measured property.
